## Introduction

In this 10-minute activity, reproduce the summary in your prepared
environment, then change a model setting and predict which targets
will run. Continue with your completed `workspace/_targets.R` and
`workspace/report.qmd`, starting from the full dataset and REML.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Get back on track {#recover-reproduce}

Run this from the project root in the **R Console** if you need to rebuild
the starting summary or repeat the exercise after changing the dataset
or estimator. Recovery selects the full 29-study dataset, backs up your
working pipeline in `workspace/`, and runs the reference pipeline with
REML. If you lost your report, copy your saved `report.qmd` back into
`workspace/` or complete the
[Quarto report exercise](06_quarto.qmd) before continuing.

``` r
source("pipelines/recover_workshop.R")
```
:::

## Step 1: rebuild from your selected input

Allow about three minutes. In the **R Console**, compare your current
summary with a rebuild in the same environment and with the same local
board. A collaborator who recreates the board can get a new version ID.
The raw and selected input checksums identify the data across boards.

```{r health-modify-reproduce, eval = FALSE}
source("pipelines/workshop_support.R")
workshop_dir <- workshop_output_dir()
pipeline_script <- file.path("workspace", "_targets.R")
pipeline_store <- file.path(workshop_dir, "_targets")
summary_path <- file.path(workshop_dir, "meta-summary.csv")
if (!file.exists(pipeline_script) || !file.exists(summary_path)) {
  stop("Run the Get back on track command at the top of this lesson.")
}

before <- read.csv(summary_path)
targets::tar_invalidate(targets::everything(), store = pipeline_store)
targets::tar_make(script = pipeline_script, store = pipeline_store)
identical(before, read.csv(summary_path))
```

Expect `TRUE`. Invalidation reruns the analysis and reuses the matching
input and model pins. A different R or *meta* version can change results.

## Step 2: make a change and predict the rebuild

Allow about four minutes. In `workspace/_targets.R`, find the `fit` target.
Change `method.tau = "REML"` to `method.tau = "DL"` and save the file.
The alternative estimator is called DerSimonian–Laird.

Predict which targets will rerun. Then compare your prediction with
the Console output.

```{r health-modify-estimator, eval = FALSE}
targets::tar_outdated(script = pipeline_script, store = pipeline_store)
targets::tar_make(script = pipeline_script, store = pipeline_store)
after <- read.csv(summary_path)
rbind(
  REML = before[, c("pooled_r", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "tau2")],
  DL = after[, c("pooled_r", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "tau2")]
)
after$pooled_r - before$pooled_r
```

Expect `pipeline_file`, `fit`, `result`, and `summary_file`. The input
checks and predictive model branch remain up to date. Both pooled
estimates round to **0.363**. Switching from REML to DL increases the
pooled correlation by about **0.00010** in this dataset. Compare how
the reported heterogeneity and intervals change in this example.

For a quick look at the recorded edit, run the command below in the
Console. Git prints a diff. An exit status of 1 means it found a
difference.

```{r health-modify-diff, eval = FALSE}
system2("git", c("--no-pager", "diff", "--no-index",
                 "pipelines/_targets_health_wellbeing.R", pipeline_script))
```

## Step 3: update the report

Allow about three minutes. Run `render_workshop_report()` in the
**R Console** and reload `workspace/report.html`. Methods now names
the DerSimonian–Laird estimator. Compare the pipeline checksum with the
new summary. The dataset ID and predictive model ID stayed the same.

## Checkpoint {#modify-checkpoint}

You reproduced the starting summary, saw a selective rebuild after an
estimator change, and rendered a report for the updated analysis.

## Optional: select a different dataset version {#change-input}

Use the general-population version to see how a new analytical input
affects both model branches. Keep your current selection so you can
restore it afterwards.

```{r health-modify-select-subset, eval = FALSE}
selection_file <- file.path(workshop_dir, "analysis-data-version.txt")
original_version <- readLines(selection_file)
versions <- read.csv(file.path(workshop_dir, "dataset-versions.csv"))
general_version <- versions$version[versions$scope == "general"]
stopifnot(length(general_version) == 1L)
writeLines(general_version, selection_file)

targets::tar_make(script = pipeline_script, store = pipeline_store)
read.csv(summary_path)[, c(
  "studies", "pooled_r", "ci_lower", "ci_upper",
  "data_version", "predictive_model_version"
)]
render_workshop_report()
```

The subset has **18 studies** and its own model pin version. The
comparison is descriptive. The full set includes these same studies,
so use a subgroup analysis to compare populations formally.

When you finish, restore the selection and render the report again.

```{r health-modify-restore-input, eval = FALSE}
writeLines(original_version, selection_file)
targets::tar_make(script = pipeline_script, store = pipeline_store)
render_workshop_report()
```
